chunks: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed to me (as executor) and ordered me to give something to an uncle of his every year. Then the uncle died.
So he (peace be upon him) wrote: Give it to his inheritors.

key_terms.أوصى إليّ: Appointed me as executor/trustee of his bequest
key_terms.الوارث: Inheritor, one who receives a deceased person's estate

ai.seo_question: What happens to an annual bequest if the beneficiary dies before the testator?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal question posed to Imam al-Baqir (or al-Jawad) about what to do when a testator's intended beneficiary — a named uncle — dies before the bequest is fully distributed. The Imam's written ruling was clear: the annual payment should continue to the uncle's heirs. This establishes the jurisprudential principle in Shia law that a bequest does not lapse merely because the named beneficiary dies; rather, it transfers to that beneficiary's inheritors, preserving the testator's charitable intent.
